name: Aether
one_liner: Launch, track and steer the coding agents on your own Aether server: see what needs you, read sessions and pull requests, and act.
description:
Aether is self-hosted software that runs coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and opencode in containers on your own server. This connector links Claude to the Aether server you are a member of, through the Aether edge at edge.onaether.dev.

Ask what needs you, what your agents did this week, or what a session changed. Read a session's conversation or terminal, its reports, diff, and its pull request's checks, reviews and comments. Search sessions and a workspace's team memory, and see which active sessions touch the same files.

With the Launch and message scope, checked by default on the consent page, launch a session on a task, message a session, answer an agent's question, pause or resume a session, and accept a session's reported success. With the Stop and approve scope, off by default, allow or deny one permission request, stop or close a session.

Who it is for: developers whose team already runs an Aether server. You need an Aether account on a server linked to the Aether edge, signed in with GitHub.

Limitations: agents run with the access your server gave them, so a launched agent can push branches and open pull requests. No connector tool installs Aether, changes server settings, merges pull requests or deletes repositories or workspaces; an agent you instruct can do what its credentials allow. Text written by agents, teammates and GitHub users is returned as untrusted data.

prerequisites: An Aether account on an Aether server linked to edge.onaether.dev, with a GitHub account bound to your member. A server under edge-access approved-devices also asks for a one-time code from aether mcp.
use_cases: Triage: ask what needs you across your sessions (agent questions, permission requests, sessions awaiting review) and answer from the chat.
Delegate: launch a session on a task in a workspace, then follow its state and reports.
Review: read what a session changed, its pull request's checks and reviewers' comments, and accept or redirect the work.
Coordinate: see which active sessions touch the same files and message a session to change course.
example_prompts: Launch a Claude Code session in the api workspace to fix the flaky login test.
Is CI green on the login fix pull request? What did reviewers say?
Which sessions touch the same files as the migration session?
Tell the parser session to use the new tokenizer.

data_handling.api_ownership: First-party: every tool calls the Aether server the user connected, through the Aether edge that 3xDevOps operates.
